subject: Measurement Invariance for Ordered Categorical Items Across Dyads

messages.author: 55bf66bb7cca8b78
messages.subject: Measurement Invariance for Ordered Categorical Items Across Dyads
parts:
Hi, 

Quick question, perhaps. Wanting to check the invariance of 15 rating scale items across married couples. I know LongInvariance in the semTools is not applicable to discrete outcomes with correlated residuals but I wanted to know more about how LongInvariance adjusts testing in the continuous outcome case to accommodate dependency between groups. I have reviewed the Vandenburg (2000) article but wanted to see if their is a more detailed reference as to what is occurring. Maybe a dumb question, but is it only that the residual covariances are freely estimated between pairs of dependent manifest variables? 

Thanks. 
John

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Measurement Invariance for Ordered Categorical Items Across Dyads
parts:
On 12/04/2015 07:23 PM, John Taylor wrote:
> residuals but I wanted to know more about how LongInvariance adjusts
> testing in the continuous outcome case to accommodate dependency between
> groups.

I believe the longInvariance() function will allow the residual
variances between the observed indicators over the timepoints/units to
be correlated. In addition, the latent variables will be correlated over
time/units.

longInvariance() returns the fitted objects for each model in a list:

FIT <- longInvariance( [your arguments] )

so you can study the parameter table of each model in turn, to see in
detail which variables are free/fixed/... For example for the second
model (the weak invariance model), you can get the parameter table as
follows:

parTable( FIT[[2]] )

and so on.

Yves.
